cases.explain: Цензура is the grammatical subject of возвращалась (was returning), so it is Nominative.

cases.sentence: Одним из проектов ___ «Да», неожиданно самым успешным, стали политические дебаты
cases.translation: One of the projects of the "Da!" movement, unexpectedly the most successful, was the political debates.
cases.explain: Движения shows possession (project of the movement), a Genitive construction.

cases.sentence: После ___ про Гунвор я потребовал раскрыть имена владельцев самого Сургутнефтегаза
cases.translation: After the question about Gunvor, I demanded that the names of Surgutneftegaz's own owners be disclosed.
cases.explain: The preposition после governs the Genitive case.

cases.sentence: Если не было пресс-релиза, причем непременно отправленного по ___, мероприятие не засчитывалось
cases.translation: If there was no press release, and one necessarily sent by fax, the event didn't count.
cases.explain: The preposition по governs the Dative case.

cases.sentence: Инвестировав даже небольшую ___, я получу возможность как акционер запрашивать у компании документы, подавать жалобы, обращаться в суд и участвовать в ежегодных собраниях
cases.translation: By investing even a small sum, I would gain the ability as a shareholder to request documents from the company, file complaints, go to court, and take part in annual meetings.
cases.explain: Сумму is the direct object of инвестировав (investing), so it is Accusative.

cases.sentence: другими молодыми активными ребятами, которые интересовались ___
cases.translation: ...with other young, active people who were interested in politics.
cases.explain: The verb интересоваться (to be interested in) governs the Instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Ты мог написать пост с ___ раздавать листовки, и реальные люди шли на реальную улицу и реально их раздавали
cases.translation: You could write a post with a call to hand out leaflets, and real people would go out onto a real street and actually hand them out.
cases.explain: The preposition с (meaning 'with') governs the Instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Находится она не в Москве, а почти в 3000 километрах от нее, в сибирском ___ Сургуте
cases.translation: It's not located in Moscow, but almost 3000 kilometers away, in the Siberian city of Surgut.
cases.explain: The preposition в indicating location governs the Prepositional case.

reading.ru: Году в 2004-м я познакомился с Марией Гайдар, дочерью ельцинского реформатора Егора Гайдара, она была членом СПС.
reading.question: Whose daughter was Maria Gaidar, whom Navalny met around 2004?
reading.correct: Yeltsin-era reformer Yegor Gaidar's daughter
reading.explain: The text identifies Maria Gaidar as the daughter of Yeltsin-era reformer Yegor Gaidar.

reading.ru: Один из символов 90-х – Владимир Жириновский, выплескивающий на Бориса Немцова стакан сока во время телевизионных дебатов, и Немцов, плещущий соком в ответ.
reading.question: What famous 1990s TV moment does Navalny mention involving Zhirinovsky and Nemtsov?
options: Zhirinovsky throwing a glass of juice at Nemtsov, and Nemtsov splashing juice back
reading.correct: Zhirinovsky throwing a glass of juice at Nemtsov, and Nemtsov splashing juice back
reading.explain: He describes Zhirinovsky splashing a glass of juice on Nemtsov during televised debates, with Nemtsov splashing juice back.

reading.ru: Эта знаменитая сцена разыгралась в 1995 году, а уже 10 лет спустя от публичных дискуссий не осталось и следа.
reading.question: According to Navalny, what had happened to public political discussion just ten years after the 1995 juice-throwing incident?
options: It had become even more popular
It became mandatory on all channels
reading.correct: It had vanished entirely
reading.explain: He writes that not a trace of public discussions remained ten years after that famous 1995 scene.

reading.ru: Площадкой для дебатов стал один из московских баров.
reading.question: Where did Navalny's political debates end up being held?
reading.correct: One of Moscow's bars
reading.explain: The text states that one of Moscow's bars became the venue for the debates.

reading.ru: Приходил, например, Дмитрий Рогозин, тогда оппозиционер, а теперь уже бывший глава Роскосмоса и преданный соратник Путина.
reading.question: What does Navalny note about Dmitry Rogozin's later career trajectory?
options: He went from opposition figure to head of Roscosmos and loyal Putin ally
He emigrated and joined the opposition abroad
reading.correct: He went from opposition figure to head of Roscosmos and loyal Putin ally
reading.explain: Navalny notes Rogozin was then an oppositionist but later became the former head of Roscosmos and a devoted ally of Putin.

reading.ru: Чем больше проект набирал популярность, тем больше это тревожило Кремль.
reading.question: How did the Kremlin react as the debate project grew more popular?
options: It offered to sponsor the debates
It ignored the project completely, permanently
reading.correct: It became increasingly worried
reading.explain: The text says the more popular the project became, the more it worried the Kremlin.

reading.ru: Проверки, полиция, угрозы отключить свет, все, чтобы они отказались сдавать нам помещение.
reading.question: What tactics were used to pressure venue owners into refusing to host the debates?
options: Inspections, police visits, and threats to cut off the electricity
reading.correct: Inspections, police visits, and threats to cut off the electricity
reading.explain: Navalny lists inspections, police, and threats to cut the electricity as pressure tactics used against venue owners.

reading.ru: Со сцены я пытался их унять, но все же это вылилось в драку, которая закончилась тем, что один из них напал на меня на улице.
reading.question: How did the provocateurs' disruption at one debate ultimately end?
options: In a fight where one of them attacked Navalny in the street
With police arresting only the provocateurs
With the debate being rescheduled peacefully
With the crowd forcing the provocateurs to leave calmly
reading.correct: In a fight where one of them attacked Navalny in the street
reading.explain: He tried to calm them from the stage, but it turned into a fight that ended with one of them attacking him on the street.

reading.ru: Нападавший оказался сыном высокопоставленного ФСБшника, и его папа не хотел раздувать скандал.
reading.question: Who turned out to be the attacker in the street fight, and why wasn't a case opened?
options: The son of a senior FSB officer, whose father didn't want a scandal
A random drunk stranger with no connections
A foreign tourist who fled the country
reading.correct: The son of a senior FSB officer, whose father didn't want a scandal
reading.explain: The attacker turned out to be the son of a high-ranking FSB officer whose father didn't want to stir up a scandal.

reading.ru: Я понял, что можно все делать без денег и без протекции Кремля.
reading.question: What key lesson did Navalny say he learned from the debate project?
options: That things could be done without money or Kremlin patronage
That television was the only effective medium
That he needed a big financial sponsor to succeed
reading.correct: That things could be done without money or Kremlin patronage
reading.explain: He says he realized everything could be done without money and without the Kremlin's patronage.

reading.ru: Российский интернет в те времена был восхитительным местом.
reading.question: How does Navalny describe the Russian internet of that era?
reading.correct: A wonderful place
reading.explain: He directly calls the Russian internet of that time a wonderful/delightful place.

reading.ru: Например, в Китае одновременно с появлением интернета стали создавать фаервол, чтобы его контролировать.
reading.question: What comparison does Navalny draw with China regarding the internet?
options: China began building a firewall to control the internet as soon as it appeared
China had no internet access until the 2010s
reading.correct: China began building a firewall to control the internet as soon as it appeared
reading.explain: He notes that in China, a firewall to control the internet was built as soon as the internet appeared, unlike in Russia.

reading.ru: Я твердо решил превратить свой ЖЖ в крупнейшее свободное СМИ в стране.
reading.question: What ambitious goal did Navalny set for his LiveJournal blog?
options: To turn it into the country's largest free media outlet
To use it only for personal diary entries
To sell it to a media company
To shut it down after a year
reading.correct: To turn it into the country's largest free media outlet
reading.explain: He firmly decided to turn his LiveJournal blog into the largest free media outlet in the country.

reading.ru: А уверен я был в том, что основа режима Путина — коррупция.
reading.question: What was Navalny firmly convinced was the foundation of Putin's regime?
reading.correct: Corruption
reading.explain: He states he was certain that the foundation of Putin's regime was corruption.

reading.ru: Инвестировав даже небольшую сумму, я получу возможность как акционер запрашивать у компании документы, подавать жалобы, обращаться в суд и участвовать в ежегодных собраниях.
reading.question: What rights did Navalny realize a small investment as a shareholder would give him?
options: The right to request documents, file complaints, sue, and attend annual meetings
The right to vote on executive salaries only
The right to a free share of profits
The right to appoint board members
reading.correct: The right to request documents, file complaints, sue, and attend annual meetings
reading.explain: He realized that even a small investment would let him request documents, file complaints, go to court, and attend annual meetings as a shareholder.

reading.ru: В представлении большинства людей это были гигантские, богатые корпорации, контролируемые государством, с которыми страшно связываться.
reading.question: How did most people view the state-controlled companies Navalny targeted?
options: As giant, rich, state-controlled corporations too scary to tangle with
As charities with no real power
reading.correct: As giant, rich, state-controlled corporations too scary to tangle with
reading.explain: Navalny says most people saw them as gigantic, rich, state-controlled corporations that were frightening to get involved with.

reading.ru: Например, в газете «Ведомости» я читал, что правительство России купило здание в центре Москвы у олигарха Вексельберга в несколько раз дороже его реальной стоимости.
reading.question: What suspicious deal did Navalny read about involving oligarch Vekselberg?
options: The Russian government bought a building from him at several times its real value
He sold shares in Rosneft below market price
He donated a building to the state for free
reading.correct: The Russian government bought a building from him at several times its real value
reading.explain: He read in the newspaper Vedomosti that the Russian government bought a building from oligarch Vekselberg for several times its real value.

reading.ru: Компания называлась «Сургутнефтегаз».
reading.question: What was the name of the company whose shareholder meeting Navalny attended in Surgut?
reading.correct: Surgutneftegaz
reading.explain: The company is explicitly named Surgutneftegaz.

reading.ru: Они могут позволить себе все, вплоть, например, до запрета местному аэропорту принимать самолет, если в нем летит человек, который им не нравится.
reading.question: How much power did Surgutneftegaz's leadership reportedly have locally?
options: They could even bar the local airport from accepting a plane carrying someone they disliked
They controlled the regional police force directly
They owned all the local media outlets
reading.correct: They could even bar the local airport from accepting a plane carrying someone they disliked
reading.explain: Navalny says they could afford anything, even down to forbidding the local airport from accepting a plane carrying someone they disliked.

reading.ru: Ей владеет ближайший друг Путина Геннадий Тимченко, и вы продаете свою нефть через нее».
reading.question: According to Navalny's question at the shareholder meeting, who owned the trading company Gunvor?
options: A Cypriot offshore fund with no known owner
reading.correct: Putin's close friend Gennady Timchenko
reading.explain: He states that Gunvor is owned by Putin's close friend Gennady Timchenko.

reading.ru: Как он посмел приехать к нам в Сургут и в открытую обвинять нас в коррупции?
reading.question: How did the people on stage seem to react, in Navalny's telling, to his questions?
options: With outrage that he dared come to Surgut and openly accuse them of corruption
With calm appreciation for his honesty
With laughter, treating it as a joke
reading.correct: With outrage that he dared come to Surgut and openly accuse them of corruption
reading.explain: He imagines their reaction as outrage: how dare he come to Surgut and openly accuse them of corruption.

reading.ru: В 2009 году я опубликовал у себя в блоге расследование «Как пилят в ВТБ».
reading.question: What was the title of the 2009 investigation Navalny published on his blog about VTB bank?
options: "How They Saw Off Money at VTB"
reading.correct: "How They Saw Off Money at VTB"
reading.explain: The investigation's title, quoted in the text, was "Как пилят в ВТБ" ("How They Saw Off Money at VTB").

reading.ru: Сам Андрей Костин, как и положено людям из ближайшего окружения Путина, был невероятно богат и не скрывал этого, несмотря на то, что банком он управлял из рук вон плохо.
reading.question: What does Navalny say about Andrei Kostin's wealth versus his management of VTB?
options: He was incredibly rich and open about it, despite managing the bank very poorly
He was modest about his wealth and managed the bank brilliantly
He had no personal wealth at all
He refused any public role despite his wealth
reading.correct: He was incredibly rich and open about it, despite managing the bank very poorly
reading.explain: Navalny says Kostin was incredibly rich and didn't hide it, even though he managed the bank very poorly.

reading.ru: И таких буровых установок было куплено не 5, не 10, а 30 штук.
reading.question: How many Chinese drilling rigs did VTB-Leasing end up purchasing, according to the investigation?
reading.explain: The text states that not 5, not 10, but 30 drilling rigs were purchased.

reading.ru: Мы с коллегами по ФБК выяснили, что за эти годы Андрей Костин подарил Аскерзаде яхту за 60 миллионов долларов, частный самолет и кучу дорогой московской недвижимости, часть из которой была куплена на деньги Государственного банка ВТБ.
reading.question: What gifts did Navalny and his FBK colleagues discover Kostin had given Asker-Zade?
options: A $60 million yacht, a private jet, and expensive Moscow real estate
A modest apartment and a used car
Only cash payments through offshore accounts
Shares in a foreign oil company
reading.correct: A $60 million yacht, a private jet, and expensive Moscow real estate
reading.explain: He and his FBK colleagues found that Kostin gave Asker-Zade a $60 million yacht, a private jet, and a lot of expensive Moscow real estate.
